scams.name: IGR Airport Transfer & Puerto Iguazú Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: IGR airport sits 17 km southeast of Puerto Iguazú and 25 km from the Iguazú Falls National Park entrance. Legitimate 2025 options: (1) pre-booked remise (private car service with posted flat rates) at ARS 25,000–30,000 (~$25 USD) one-way to Puerto Iguazú town per r/argentina 'IGR airport to Puerto Iguazu' (2025) and r/AskArgentina 'Transporte del aeropuerto a Puerto Iguazú de noche' (2025); (2) VES-style shuttle vans at ARS 6,000–10,000 per person; (3) hotel shuttle if staying at Loi Suites / Hotel Saint George / Awasi Iguazu (verify booking confirmation). The scam patterns: arrivals-hall 'private transfer' touts quote ARS 60,000–100,000 one-way (2.5–4x legitimate), claiming 'fixed flat rate' and 'airport-approved'; hotel-concierge 'VIP transfer' upsells at $80–$150 USD one-way for the same 20-min run; Belmond / premium-hotel desks quote what r/travel 'Iguazu transport from IGR to Brazil' (2024) OP called 'absurd' rates. For older travelers in Puerto Iguazú, the clean playbook: (1) pre-book remise with your hotel before arrival — verify ARS price in writing via WhatsApp, and confirm driver's name + license plate + arrival time; (2) alternative: official IGR airport-taxi counter inside arrivals with posted flat-rate chart (ARS 25,000–30,000 to town), and pay via card if accepted; (3) for IGR → Foz do Iguaçu (Brazilian side, requires border crossing), book a cross-border remise at ARS 55,000 round-trip ($55 USD) — verify the driver stops at both migraciones posts (Argentine exit + Brazilian entry) to get legal entry/exit stamps; (4) within Puerto Iguazú town for short hops, use remise (taxi with radio dispatch) and confirm price before starting trip — most trips within town are ARS 3,000–8,000. For the border-crossing leg specifically: unlicensed taxi drivers frequently skip migraciones stamps to save 15 minutes, which creates overstay exit-fine exposure (~$100 USD) when you leave Brazil or Argentina later. r/AskArgentina 'Me voy a Ciudad del Este, recomendaciones de' (2025) documents this pattern, and r/ExpatFIRE 'Paraguay' (2023) documents Ciudad del Este taxi drivers attempting bag theft during triple-frontier crossings. Always insist on both stamps, photograph both stamps, and never accept a driver's 'it's faster without' reasoning. Save Comisaría Seccional 1ra Puerto Iguazú (Av. Victoria Aguirre, +54 3757 619784, 24/7) and 911.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book IGR airport remise via your hotel before arrival — verify ARS price in writing via WhatsApp, confirm driver's name + license plate + arrival time, and pay via card at drop-off not cash Alternative: use the official IGR airport-taxi counter inside arrivals with posted flat-rate chart (ARS 25,000–30,000 to Puerto Iguazú town) — pay via card if accepted, get printed recibo For IGR → Foz do Iguaçu (Brazilian side) book a cross-border remise at ARS 55,000 round-trip (~$55 USD) — insist driver stops at both migraciones posts and photograph both entry/exit stamps on your passport Refuse all arrivals-hall 'private transfer' / 'flat rate' / 'airport-approved' touts quoting above ARS 30,000 — walk past them to the official taxi counter or meet your pre-booked remise Save Comisaría Seccional 1ra Puerto Iguazú (Av. Victoria Aguirre, +54 3757 619784, 24/7) + ITUREM complaint line (+54 3757 554545) in phone before arrival
scams.location: Cataratas del Iguazú International Airport (IGR), Puerto Iguazú downtown taxi ranks (Av. Victoria Aguirre, Terminal de Ómnibus), hotel-concierge transfer desks, Sheraton Iguazú / Gran Meliá Iguazú in-park hotel booking

scams.name: Iguazú National Park Tour Package & Gran Aventura Upsell
scams.description: Iguazú Falls National Park (Argentine side) is Argentina's crown-jewel UNESCO site with ~1.5 million annual visitors. 2025 foreigner entrance fee: ARS 45,000 (~$32 USD, effective 2025-01-06) per argentina.gob.ar/parquesnacionales, paid at the park gate — Includes all walkway circuits (Upper, Lower, Garganta del Diablo) and the Tren Ecológico de la Selva (reopened 2024-07-13 after the November 2023 flood closure). The park entrance does not include boat tours, jeep rides, or guided tours — these are separate operator products sold in-park by Iguazú Jungle, the sole official concessionaire. Iguazú Jungle 2025 product rates at tickets.iguazujungle.com: Gran Aventura (4x4 jungle + zodiac-boat under-falls) ARS 70,000 (~$50 USD); Macuco Safari ARS 45,000; Paseo Ecológico (quiet-boat upper-river) ARS 35,000. The scam ecosystem targets tourists at two points. First: Puerto Iguazú downtown travel agencies (Av. Victoria Aguirre + Av. Brasil strips) and hotel concierges sell 'VIP Iguazú Day' packages at $150–$300 USD/person that bundle the $32 park entrance + $50 Gran Aventura + $20 transfer into a $150+ product with a 2–3x markup. Second: Viator / GetYourGuide / third-party booking sites sell 'Iguazú Falls Skip-the-Line' listings at $100–$180 USD claiming priority access — There is NO skip-the-line product at Iguazú; you still queue at the gate for the same ticket. Per r/travel 'Iguazu Falls, which side has the better boat tour?' (2023), the Brazilian-side Macuco Safari boat is separately criticized as 'borderline a scam' when water levels are low (advertised under-falls run becomes a distant wave), but Argentine-side Gran Aventura is legitimate and recommended. The defensive playbook for older travelers: (1) buy park entrance direct at the gate or via iguazuargentina.com official site — ARS 45,000 foreigner; (2) book Gran Aventura direct at tickets.iguazujungle.com or at the in-park Iguazú Jungle booth (located near the Cataratas Station of the Tren Ecológico) — ARS 70,000 adult; do not prebook via Viator/GetYourGuide at $120+ USD markup; (3) for Garganta del Diablo circuit (the main viewing platform over the main cataract): the last Tren Ecológico train departs Garganta at 17:30, plan 3–4 hours to do all three circuits; (4) avoid 'Iguazú Falls Skip-the-Line' and 'Private Guide Priority Access' third-party products — these do not exist; (5) budget one full day for Argentine side + half-day for Brazilian side (Parque Nacional do Iguaçu, separate entrance BRL 131 foreigner, requires border crossing).
scams.avoidance: Buy park entrance direct at the gate or via iguazuargentina.com — ARS 45,000 foreigner (2025), includes all walkway circuits + Tren Ecológico Book Gran Aventura direct at tickets.iguazujungle.com or at the in-park Iguazú Jungle booth (near Cataratas Station) — ARS 70,000 adult; not via third-party resellers For Garganta del Diablo, board Tren Ecológico at Cataratas Station before 16:00 — Last train departs Garganta at 17:30; plan 3–4 hours total for all three circuits (Upper, Lower, Garganta) For Brazilian side (Foz do Iguaçu) book independent cross-border remise to Parque Nacional do Iguaçu (BRL 131 foreigner entrance at the gate) — avoid 'both sides one-day' bundles from Puerto Iguazú agencies quoting $250+ USD Verify tour operator has current Iguazú Jungle authorization (official concessionaire badge) before paying — only Iguazú Jungle can sell in-park boat/jeep products
scams.location: Iguazú Falls National Park main entrance (Centro de Visitantes), Argentine-side park concessionaire Iguazú Jungle (Gran Aventura / Macuco Safari / Paseo Ecológico), hotel-concierge tour desks, Puerto Iguazú downtown travel agency strips (Av. Victoria Aguirre, Av. Brasil)

scams.name: Puerto Iguazú Hotel & In-Park Lodge Booking Fraud
scams.description: Puerto Iguazú's accommodation market has two tiers with very different scam profiles. Premium in-park: Gran Meliá Iguazú (formerly Sheraton Iguazú Resort, rebranded 2024) is the only hotel inside the national park with direct walkway access to the Cataratas — ~$640 USD/night on Expedia 2026 dates, rates $246–$1 USD,350 depending on view/season. Premium town-side: Loi Suites Iguazú, Awasi Iguazu (ultra-premium lodge), Hotel Saint George. Mid-range town: Hotel Saint George, Jasy Hotel, Orquideas Palace. Budget: multiple hostels + Airbnbs near Tres Fronteras. Common scam variants: (1) 'corporate rate' emails claiming to be from Gran Meliá Iguazú / Loi Suites offering 40–60% discount via intermediary booking agent — all premium Iguazú properties book only via their official websites or direct phone reservations, never via third-party 'booking agent' emails; (2) Airbnb fake listings near Tres Fronteras demanding 30–50% USD cash deposit 'off-platform' via Western Union or USDT — these listings are often photo-stolen from legitimate properties; (3) WhatsApp / Instagram / Facebook Marketplace 'Puerto Iguazú direct rental' offers from sellers claiming to own cabañas on Av. Tres Fronteras — verify via Google Street View of the address and reverse-image-search the photos; (4) 'Sheraton Iguazú' typo-squat domain emails still circulating months after the Gran Meliá rebrand, directing deposits to fraudulent accounts. The safer path for older travelers is (1) book all accommodation via Booking.com / Hotels.com / Airbnb platform payment with full platform protection — never off-platform wire or crypto deposits; (2) for premium in-park stay, book Gran Meliá Iguazú direct at melia.com or marriott.com legacy Sheraton page (which auto-redirects to Meliá as of 2024 rebrand) — verify URL matches TripAdvisor/Booking.com listing link; (3) for Awasi Iguazu ultra-premium book direct at awasi.com — verify booking confirmation includes full itinerary + meals + guide; (4) mid-range: Loi Suites / Hotel Saint George via Booking.com platform payment; (5) verify every Airbnb has 50+ reviews + 'verified host' badge + photos that pass Google reverse-image-search; (6) refuse all 'discount' / 'corporate rate' / 'direct wire' offers from anyone claiming to be a 'booking agent' for a premium Iguazú property. Save Comisaría Seccional 1ra Puerto Iguazú (+54 3757 619784).
scams.avoidance: Book all Puerto Iguazú accommodation via Booking.com / Hotels.com / Airbnb platform payment in full — never off-platform wire or crypto deposits, even for 'verified' listings For in-park Gran Meliá Iguazú book direct at melia.com — verify URL matches TripAdvisor/Booking.com listing link, and confirm the 'Sheraton' legacy auto-redirects to Meliá as of 2024 rebrand For Awasi Iguazu ultra-premium lodge book direct at awasi.com with full meal + guide + transfer inclusive booking confirmation — never via 'travel agent' intermediary Verify every Airbnb has 50+ reviews + 'verified host' / 'Superhost' badge + photos that pass Google reverse-image-search — Tres Fronteras photo-stolen listings are the #1 Puerto Iguazú STR scam Refuse all 'discount' / 'corporate rate' / 'direct wire' offers from anyone claiming to be a 'booking agent' — Gran Meliá / Loi Suites / Awasi / Saint George sell only direct or via platform
scams.location: Puerto Iguazú downtown hotels + STRs (Av. Victoria Aguirre, Av. Brasil, Tres Fronteras), in-park Gran Meliá Iguazú (formerly Sheraton Iguazú Resort — the only hotel inside Iguazú National Park), Awasi Iguazu / Loi Suites Iguazú / Hotel Saint George premium-segment off-platform fraud targets

scams.name: Triple Frontier (Tres Fronteras) Border-Crossing Scams
scams.description: The Triple Frontier (Tres Fronteras) where Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay meet is a signature Puerto Iguazú experience — the Argentine monument viewpoint is a 5-min taxi ride from downtown and free to visit. But the 'Triple Frontier Day Trip' that crosses all three borders to visit Ciudad del Este's electronics markets is one of Argentina's riskiest tourist experiences per r/ExpatFIRE 'Paraguay' (2023) and r/AskArgentina 'Me voy a Ciudad del Este, recomendaciones de' (2025). The scam patterns to watch include: (1) Puerto Iguazú travel agencies selling 'Ciudad del Este Shopping Day' at $80–$150 USD/person with drivers who deliberately skip migraciones stamps to save time — this creates $100+ USD overstay exit-fines at your eventual Argentina or Brazil departure when the missing entry stamps are flagged; (2) Ciudad del Este taxi drivers at the border attempting bag grabs during the Puente de la Amistad crossing chaos — r/ExpatFIRE OP documented a driver who attempted to steal their bags during transfer; (3) 'Triple frontier photo spot' scams where unofficial 'guides' demand $10–$30 USD for access to the Hito monument viewpoint (entrance is free — it's a public municipal park); (4) Paraguayan street money-changers at the border offering 'better rate' that always involves counterfeit Paraguayan Guaraní or short-changed USD. The safer path for older travelers: (1) visit the Argentine Tres Fronteras monument (Hito Tres Fronteras) for the photo — it's a free municipal viewpoint at the end of Av. Tres Fronteras in Puerto Iguazú, 5-min taxi from downtown, no tour needed; (2) if you want to see Brazilian-side Foz do Iguaçu attractions (Itaipu Dam, Bird Park), book a cross-border remise at ARS 55,000 round-trip ($55 USD) with insistence on both migraciones stamps and photograph each stamp; (3) skip Ciudad del Este entirely — per r/ExpatFIRE 'Paraguay' (2023) the electronics markets there are high-crime, counterfeit-heavy, and known for bag theft / overcharge / counterfeit currency; the 10-20% discount on electronics vs. Buenos Aires is not worth the security risk for tourists; (4) never exchange money at border street-stands — use Western Union in Puerto Iguazú (Av. Victoria Aguirre) for USD-to-peso or USD-to-real at bank rates; (5) carry photocopies of passport with entry/exit stamps, not the physical passport, across any border casual crossing. The Ciudad del Este security environment is a serious consideration for older travelers — r/ExpatFIRE 'Paraguay' (2023) describes bag-grab attempts at the Puente de la Amistad, and r/AskArgentina 'Me voy a Ciudad del Este' (2025) documents illegal tout-led crossings without stamps. Always carry your passport in a zipped internal pocket, never visible; travel with a small day-bag only; and do not accept transport offers from anyone approaching you inside the Ciudad del Este side of the bridge. Save Comisaría Seccional 1ra Puerto Iguazú (+54 3757 619784) and the Argentine embassy in Asunción (+595 21 210-683) before crossing.
scams.avoidance: Visit Argentine Hito Tres Fronteras monument (end of Av. Tres Fronteras, 5-min taxi from downtown Puerto Iguazú) — it's free, well-maintained, and has the classic three-flags photo; no tour required For Brazilian-side Foz do Iguaçu attractions, book a cross-border remise at ARS 55,000 round-trip ($55 USD) — insist driver stops at both Argentine migraciones (exit) and Brazilian migraciones (entry), photograph both stamps Skip Ciudad del Este entirely — per r/ExpatFIRE 'Paraguay' (2023) the electronics markets there are high-crime, counterfeit-heavy, with bag-theft documented; the 10-20% electronics savings vs. Buenos Aires is not worth the security risk Never exchange money at border street-stands — use Western Union in Puerto Iguazú (Av. Victoria Aguirre) for USD-to-peso or USD-to-real conversion at posted bank rates with zero counterfeit risk If you must cross into Ciudad del Este, travel with passport in zipped internal pocket (not visible), small day-bag only, and photocopies of stamped passport pages — never accept transport from anyone approaching you inside the bridge
scams.location: Hito Tres Fronteras viewpoint (Puerto Iguazú), Tancredo Neves International Bridge (Argentina–Brazil), Puente de la Amistad (Argentina–Paraguay via Brazil), Ciudad del Este border-market tour operators, Puerto Iguazú downtown 'triple-frontier day trip' travel agency sellers

scams.name: Puerto Iguazú Downtown Tour-Agency Overcharge & 'Both Sides One Day' Bundles
scams.description: Puerto Iguazú downtown has 40+ travel agencies along Av. Victoria Aguirre and Av. Brasil selling packaged day-trip products to Iguazú Falls (both sides), Itaipu Dam, Bird Park (Parque das Aves Foz do Iguaçu), and Triple Frontier. These agencies operate legitimately but universally mark up direct-book products by 30–100%. The 'VIP Iguazú Full Experience' packages run $250–$500 USD/person for a combination that costs $100–$150 USD when booked individually: (1) ARS 45,000 Argentine park entrance = $32 USD; (2) ARS 70,000 Iguazú Jungle Gran Aventura = $50 USD; (3) Cross-border remise to Foz do Iguaçu = $15 USD; (4) BRL 131 Brazilian park entrance = $27 USD; (5) Optional BRL 90 Bird Park entrance = $18 USD. Total DIY: ~$142 USD — Vs. Agency bundle at $350+. A specific 'Both Sides One Day' bundle is particularly popular and particularly inefficient. The pattern: agency promises 'See Argentine + Brazilian falls + Triple Frontier in 10 hours' at $180–$280 USD/person. In practice: you get 2.5 hours at Argentine side (not enough for Garganta + Upper + Lower circuits with Tren Ecológico), 1.5 hours at Brazilian side (barely enough for the walkway), 30 minutes rushed at Triple Frontier monument, and 2+ hours lost to border-crossing queues + transfers. The Argentine side alone deserves a full 6–8 hour day to do all three circuits; r/travel 'Iguazu Falls, which side has the better boat tour?' (2023) and r/travel 'IGR to Iguazu Falls' (2024) both strongly advise spending one full day on each side. The safer approach for older travelers: (1) allocate minimum 2 days to Iguazú — Day 1 Argentine side (6–8 hours, all three circuits + optional Gran Aventura), Day 2 Brazilian side (4–5 hours, walkway + Macuco Safari if water is high + optional Itaipu/Bird Park); (2) book park entrances direct at iguazuargentina.com (ARS 45,000) and at the Brazilian park gate (BRL 131); (3) book Gran Aventura direct at tickets.iguazujungle.com (ARS 70,000); (4) arrange cross-border remise via your hotel at ARS 55,000 round-trip ($55 USD) with migraciones stops; (5) skip all 'Both Sides One Day' / 'VIP Iguazú Full Experience' agency bundles — you pay 2–3x for a worse experience; (6) if you need a walking guide for the park (recommended for first-time visitors), hire a private Spanish-English guide at the park Centro de Visitantes for ARS 40,000–80,000 ($30–$60 USD) for 3 hours — Versus agency 'VIP Private Guide' at $150–$300 for identical service.
scams.avoidance: Allocate minimum 2 days — Day 1 Argentine side (6–8 hours for all three circuits + Gran Aventura), Day 2 Brazilian side (4–5 hours for walkway + optional Itaipu/Bird Park) Book park entrances direct at iguazuargentina.com (ARS 45,000 foreigner, 2025) and at the Brazilian park gate (BRL 131 foreigner) — skip all third-party 'entrance included' bundles Book Iguazú Jungle Gran Aventura direct at tickets.iguazujungle.com (ARS 70,000, 2025) — the only official boat+jeep concessionaire; not via Viator/GetYourGuide at $120+ markup Arrange cross-border remise via your hotel at ARS 55,000 round-trip (~$55 USD) with confirmed migraciones stops at both borders — Not via 'Both Sides Tour' bundle If you want a walking guide, hire a private Spanish-English guide at the park Centro de Visitantes for ARS 40,000–80,000 ($30–$60) for 3 hours — Versus agency 'VIP Private Guide' at $150–$300 for identical service
scams.location: Puerto Iguazú downtown travel agency strips (Av. Victoria Aguirre, Av. Brasil, Calle Hipólito Yrigoyen), hotel-concierge tour desks at Jasy Hotel / Hotel Saint George / Orquideas Palace, Viator / GetYourGuide / Civitatis third-party booking listings

scams.name: Puerto Iguazú Restaurant Bill-Padding & Tourist-Menu Overcharge
scams.description: Puerto Iguazú tourist restaurants use the standard Argentine cubierto and propina sugerida system. The Av. Victoria Aguirre and Av. Brasil strips aggressively pad bills with unlisted cubiertos, 'bottled water included' surprises, and surprise 'servicio especial' charges beyond the posted menu. The specific Puerto Iguazú restaurant-scam patterns: (1) unlisted cubierto at $5,000+ ARS/person added to the bill (cubierto must be disclosed on the printed menu before ordering under Argentine consumer-protection law — an unlisted cubierto can be refused); (2) surprise 'aperitivo' or 'panera especial' or 'bottled water included' items appearing on bill for items you didn't order; (3) tourist-menu vs. Locals-menu dual pricing where the tourist-facing menu shows items at 40–60% markup over the Spanish-only menu staff carry separately; (4) 'servicio incluido' (service included) or 'propina obligatoria' (mandatory tip) language added to bills without menu disclosure — these are not legal under Argentine law; (5) wine-list fabrication where the bottle price is invented on the spot rather than from a printed list — Common in Selva misiones jungle-lodge restaurants where 'local bottle' runs $80+ USD. A prudent approach for older travelers: (1) request the menu before seating and verify cubierto disclosure is printed on the menu — refuse any unlisted cubierto on the bill; (2) if you see both a Spanish-only menu and an English/tourist menu, ASK specifically for the Spanish menu (or photograph both and compare prices — 30%+ discrepancy is a tourist-menu scam); (3) photograph the menu page with your phone before ordering — this is your evidence if the bill arrives with surprise items; (4) 'propina sugerida' is optional not mandatory — 10% tip is standard but service staff cannot enforce it; 'propina obligatoria' / 'servicio incluido' added without menu disclosure can be formally disputed; (5) pay with card (chargeback protection) rather than USD cash — foreign cards in 2025 auto-apply MEP-equivalent rate via Argentina's tourist-card scheme; (6) report persistent bill-padding to Defensoría del Consumidor Misiones (+54 3752 447-100) and ITUREM (Iguazú Turismo Ente Municipal, +54 3757 554545); (7) consider dining at hotel restaurant (Gran Meliá Iguazú / Loi Suites) where menu disclosure is tighter and cubierto practices are consistent with international hospitality standards.
scams.avoidance: Request the menu before seating and verify cubierto disclosure ($1,500–$3,500 ARS/person typical) is printed on the menu — refuse any unlisted cubierto on the bill Ask for the Spanish-only menu if staff hand you a separate English/tourist menu — 30%+ price discrepancy indicates tourist-menu scam Photograph the menu page with your phone before ordering — this is your evidence against surprise bill-padding Pay with foreign credit card for MEP-equivalent tourist-card rate auto-application + chargeback protection — Not USD cash Report persistent bill-padding to Defensoría del Consumidor Misiones (+54 3752 447-100) and ITUREM Iguazú Turismo (+54 3757 554545)
scams.location: Av. Victoria Aguirre tourist restaurant strip (Puerto Iguazú), Av. Brasil waterfront restaurants, Calle Córdoba pedestrian tourist dining zone, hotel restaurant at Gran Meliá Iguazú / Loi Suites / Hotel Saint George, Selva misiones jungle-lodge restaurants
